newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Dec 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- South Africa's long-term foreign debt falling due next year would be about $1.1 billion more than this year at about $2.9 billion -- a bill which could put severe pressure on the country's foreign exchange reserves.

- About 11,000 claims for land restitution by victims of apartheid dispossession are outstanding, prompting government moves to accelerate the restitution process through legislation and other measures.
- Gauteng's first matric exams under a single nonracial education department failed to produce improved results this year.

- Thousands of Christmas callers could be hit hard by large telephone bills next year as Telkom did not charge special reduced rates on Christmas Day or the Day of Goodwill -- nor will it on New Year's Day.

- The number of firearms stolen from police, the defence force, security companies and individuals more than doubled to 35,778 this year from 16,002 last year, says South African Police Service spokesman Snr Supt Andrew Lesch.

- Alleged cheating by 1,413 pupils who wrote the Gauteng Education Department matric exams had a negligible effect on the results, with the top 100 pupils of the Class of '96 producing brilliant marks.
- Justice Minister Dullah Omar yesterday suggested a double bomb attack on Christmas shoppers which killed three people, including two children, could have been the work of the far right wing.
- Seven people were killed and 87 injured when a lorry carrying holiday-makers rolled on the N1-north about 23 kilometres south of Pietersburg in Northern Province yesterday.
